title: Reroute circuit investigation journal
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs for the 2026-03-08 latency/redirect spike where traffic from eu-west-1 started being sent to us-west-2 for ~3h. This is my scratchpad — half commands, half hypotheses.

High-level summary (quick):
- Symptom: sustained 200–700ms extra P99 for a subset of customer routes (mainly low-tenancy bursty chat requests).
- Observed: a non-zero fraction of requests were routed across regions (eu -> us) instead of local EU pool. No errors returned to callers, just higher latency and increased egress costs.
- Window: ~2026-03-08T03:12Z -> 2026-03-08T06:45Z.

What I actually saw (raw):
- Router metrics: route_reroute_count{region="eu-west-1",target_region="us-west-2"} spiked from 0.0001 to 0.07 of total routes for some customers.
- Route policy TTLs: several policies showed TTL evaluation misses in logs ("policy-eval: TTL-mismatch: route=R-1123 ttl=0s")
- Edge logs (gateway-router stdout):
  [2026-03-08T03:13:02Z] router: info: accept req id=abc123 tenant=T-77 route=R-1123 selected_backend=pool-eu-1
  [2026-03-08T03:13:02Z] router: warn: re-evaluated route id=R-1123 => failover_policy=route-rehandshake, target=us-west-2 reason="pool-threshold-exceeded"
  [2026-03-08T03:13:03Z] egress: notice: handoff connection reset by peer (ERR_RESET) to pool-eu-1 node=node-eu-3

Commands I ran (notes + output snippets):
- kubectl tail of router pod (namespace=inference):
  kubectl -n inference logs gw-router-5d8f -c router --since=4h | grep "re-evaluated route" | head -n 20\  # saw ~2k lines where router flipped target_region

- Inspect route state via internal CLI (rictl):
  rictl routes inspect R-1123 --history --since 2026-03-08T02:00Z
  # output (abridged):
  # 2026-03-08T03:12:57Z: eval -> selected pool=pool-eu-1 load=0.82 capacity=18/20
  # 2026-03-08T03:13:02Z: re-eval -> pool-threshold-exceeded (threshold=0.8) fallback -> pool-us-2

- TCP dump for a single client IP (to verify connection establishment/handshake):
  sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.14.22.53 and port 443 -w /tmp/eu-client.pcap (started 03:05Z)
  # pcap shows initial SYN->SYN/ACK to pool-eu-1 then short RSTs from pool nodes ~10s later; router re-initiates to US pool.

- Node metrics (node-eu-3):
  ssh jump@node-eu-3 -- journalctl -u container-runtime | tail -n 200
  # saw: oom-kill of process 'infer-worker' at 03:12:50Z sudden mem spike (approx 1.9GiB > 1.7GiB limit) -> kernel oom. Node marked unschedulable by autoscaler.

Error snippets and telemetry (copy/paste raw-ish):
- router log: "re-evaluated route id=R-1123 => failover_policy=route-rehandshake, target=us-west-2 reason=\"pool-threshold-exceeded\""
- egress log: "ERR_CONN_RESET after 102ms to node-eu-3 (code=ECONNRESET)"
- orchestration: "autoscaler: draining node-eu-3 due to OOM; evicted pods=4 route-affinity=soft"
- cache: "prefix-cache: hit=false key=tenant:T-77/prefix:0x9f2 ttl=0"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Autoscaler-caused transient capacity loss: node OOM -> drain -> pool load increased above threshold -> router re-evaluated route policy -> rehandshake -> cross-region target selected. Likely.
2) Route TTL mis-evaluation combined with clock skew: some router instances reported TTL=0 for policy lookups (see TTL-mismatch log), causing aggressive reroute. Could be caused by config propagation delay or bad clock on a control-plane host.
3) Stale KV cache in router leading to incorrect pool capacity numbers (cache stale for ~60s so router thought eu pool was full).
4) DNS/edge egress flapping (less likely): quick RSTs observed but those correlate with oom event above.

What I tried to verify each hypothesis: 
- For #1 (autoscaler): pulled node-level metrics + autoscaler events. Confirmed OOM at 03:12:50Z and a drain event at 03:12:52Z. Checked PRS: autoscaler velocity looked normal but node resource pressure spiked due to unbounded worker mem in infer-worker.
- For #2 (TTL/clock): ran ntpstat on control-plane and 3 router hosts. ntpstat was OK on 2/3; one host (gw-router-7) showed offset 420ms. Also saw "TTL-mismatch" logs primarily on gw-router-7.
- For #3 (KV cache): forced a cache invalidation on a staging router: rictl cache invalidate prefix tenant:T-77 — then watched requests, they correctly stayed local. But I can't force invalidate prod without risk.

Short repro plan (safe):
1) On staging: simulate node drain by killing infer-worker on one eu pool node and observe route_rehandshake count.
2) Reproduce TTL-mismatch by temporarily shifting control-plane clock by ~500ms on a staging router instance. Verify policy eval logs.
3) Measure cache TTL and staleness window by introducing controlled capacity changes and recording router decisions.

Immediate remediation ideas (for on-call):
- Temporarily raise pool-threshold in routing config for eu pools to 0.85 -> 0.9 to avoid immediate cross-region handoffs during noisy drains. (low-risk, revert after incident)
- Add a short suppression window (30s) after node drain notifications where router will prefer local pool for same tenant if cache says available.
- Add alert rule: when route_reroute_count to other region > 0.02 for >5m for core-customer set -> page infra-routing.

Open things / TODO (personal):
- [ ] Confirm whether eviction was caused by a regression in recent infer-worker memory allocation (check PRs around 2026-03-07).
- [ ] Audit code path that sets policy TTL to ensure default TTL != 0 on config error.
- [ ] Add more granular telemetry: tag reroute events with "trigger_reason" (oom/threshold/ttl/cache/mismatch).
- [ ] Draft short KB for CS explaining cross-region handoffs and cost/latency implications.

Notes to self:
- Watch the PR that changed infer-worker alloc heuristics (GH #409) — high chance it's related.
- Be careful when invalidating cache in prod. Prefer draining test pools first.

Quick timeline (hand scribble):
- 03:12:49Z - infer-worker memory spike on node-eu-3
- 03:12:50Z - kernel OOM, infer-worker killed
- 03:12:52Z - autoscaler marks node-eu-3 unschedulable + drain
- 03:12:57Z - pool-eu-1 available capacity drops below threshold (0.82 -> 0.68)
- 03:13:02Z - router re-evaluates routes -> selects us-west-2 for some tenants
- 03:13:05Z - customers start seeing elevated P99
- 06:45:00Z - traffic normalizes as nodes come back and autoscaler stabilizes

Quick checklist for followups with SRE/serving-runtime teams:
- Confirm fix for infer-worker mem regression (if present) + rollout plan (hotfix vs revert).
- Plan to add TTL/clock skew detection to routing control plane logs.
- Run staging replays of the scenario to validate suppression heuristics don't break capacity isolation.

End of scratchpad. If I forget: ping Marco for the pcap and Ethan for the autoscaler debug dump.

-- Priya
